auditPolicy.ciBehavior: The raw audit runs as its own security-audit job in CI so a functional regression and the known security-policy gate are separately attributable. That job still fails, so the workflow reports red.
auditPolicy.futureTask: A controlled mechanism distinguishing reviewed temporary exceptions from new vulnerabilities, without hiding the raw audit result. Still not built.

validation.uuidLengthCheckFinding: The exact 36-character length check in requireId is redundant defence-in-depth, not the mechanism that rejects trailing line terminators. The anchored pattern already rejects \n, \r, U+2028 and U+2029 because it ends with the specific class [0-9a-f]{12}. Both checks retained; an earlier claim that the length check rejects a trailing newline was corrected.

stage23.scope: Internal session primitives only: token generation and hashing, create, validate, revoke, revoke-all. No HTTP wiring.
concurrencyLimitations: A session insert racing an account disable can succeed; validation independently rechecks current status.
Creation committing outside the revoke-all update snapshot can survive that revoke-all.
In-flight validation can race with later revocation or disabling; the returned context is not a perpetual authorization grant.
Disabling is not implicit revocation; re-enabling a user can make an otherwise valid, unrevoked, unexpired session usable again.

correctionsMade: Corrected an inaccurate claim in tasks/CURRENT.md: the 36-character UUID length check is redundant defence-in-depth and does not reject trailing newlines; the anchored regex already does. Verified empirically against the compiled service.

Added a unit test pinning the rejected identifier shapes across all four JavaScript line terminators plus truncation, extension, braces and urn:uuid: prefixes, and asserting a genuine uppercase UUID reaches the database so rejection cannot pass vacuously.

Added an integration test for the documented disable/re-enable behaviour, which had no coverage: disabling rejects with USER_DISABLED, re-enabling restores the session with its original absolute expiry, and expiry is still enforced afterwards.

Updated tasks/completed/README.md, which indexed only Stages 0 and 1, to also index the hosted CI repair, Stage 2.1 and the newly archived Stage 2.2 handoff, and to state that Stage 2 as a whole is not accepted.
